desc:
Given an integer array nums with at least three elements (any order) and an integer target, choose three elements at three different positions so that their sum is as close to target as possible. Return that sum.

If two different sums are equally close to the target, return the smaller one.

nums = [4, -2, 7, 1, -5], target = 10
best triple: -2 + 4 + 7 = 9 (distance 1); 1 + 4 + 7 = 12 is farther away
result = 9
hints: Three nested loops give O(n³). Fix one element and see what is left to solve.
With the first element fixed, you need the pair among the remaining elements whose sum is closest to target - nums[i]. That is the sorted closest-pair problem.
Sort once. For every index i run lo = i + 1, hi = n - 1, compare each triple sum with the best one by (distance, sum), and move the pointer that brings the sum toward the target.
editorial: Sort the array. For each index i, sweep the suffix after it with two pointers lo and hi. The current sum is s = a[i] + a[lo] + a[hi]. Compare the key (|s - target|, s) to the best key found so far; the second component implements the tie rule. If s < target increase lo, if s > target decrease hi, and if s == target return it at once.

The discarding argument is the same as for two sums: if s is below the target, no partner of a[lo] inside the window can give a bigger sum than a[hi] does, so a[lo] is useless for this i. Total time is O(n²) with O(1) extra space, versus O(n³) for brute force.
Pitfall: remember that the three elements must come from different positions, so the pointers always stay strictly to the right of i and lo < hi.
